CoreASEC 3103

Agricultural Marketing and Trade

Syllabus

Introduction:


This course is designed to equip students with
comprehensive knowledge of agricultural marketing systems, market structure,
pricing mechanisms, market channels, and India's agricultural trade policies.
Students will understand how farm produce moves from producer to consumer, the
role of government institutions (APMC, FCI, CWC, NAFED), international trade
frameworks (WTO, AoA, GATT), and emerging digital marketing platforms. The
course integrates theory with practical exposure through market visits, data
collection, and analysis of real-world commodity price behaviour.



Course Objective:


The objectives of the course are
1.     To understand
the fundamentals of agricultural marketing and trade.


2.     To analyze
the factors influencing supply and demand in agricultural markets.


3.     To explore
different marketing channels and strategies in agriculture.


4.     To examine
the role of government policies and regulations in agricultural markets.


To introduce students to international trade
frameworks and India's participation in global agricultural markets.



Course Outcomes:


After completion of the course
students will be able to:
•

CO1: Explain the fundamental concepts of agricultural marketing
— definitions, scope, functions, importance, and the marketing mix for farm
produce.
•

CO2: Analyse demand and supply dynamics, price behaviour, price
spread, marketing costs, and margins for selected agricultural commodities.
•

CO3: Evaluate different marketing channels, market integration,
and the role of market functionaries and institutions in agricultural marketing
in India.
•

CO4: Examine government policies, regulatory frameworks (APMC
Acts, Model APMC Act), and the role of public sector institutions (FCI, CWC,
NAFED, SWC) in agricultural marketing.
•

CO5: Assess India's agricultural trade policies, international
trade concepts (comparative advantage, absolute advantage), WTO framework,
Agreement on Agriculture (AoA), and India's trade performance in
agri-commodities.

Syllabus
Module I: Concepts and
Fundamentals of Agricultural Marketing


Theory:
Definitions of market, marketing, agricultural marketing; Market
structure, marketing mix and market segmentation; Classification and
characteristics of agricultural markets; Demand, supply and producer's surplus
of agri-commodities: nature and determinants; Marketable and marketed surplus —
meaning, factors affecting; Pricing considerations: cost-based,
competition-based; Market promotion — advertising, personal selling, sales
promotion, publicity; Merits and demerits of agricultural marketing.
Practical:
Plotting and study of demand and supply curves; Calculation of
elasticities; Study of relationship between market arrivals and prices of
selected commodities.
Thrust Area (Practice
Sessions 1-2): Supply-Demand Curves, Elasticity, and Market Price Analysis


 
Module II: Marketing
Process, Channels, and Market Functions


Theory:
Marketing process and functions — concentration, dispersion,
equalization, exchange functions, buying, selling; Physical functions —
storage, transport, processing; Facilitating functions — packaging, branding,
grading, quality control, labelling (Agmark); Market functionaries: types,
importance, role of different agencies; Marketing channels: types, integration,
efficiency, cost and price spread; Marketing costs, margins and price spread;
Factors affecting cost of marketing; Reasons for higher marketing costs.
Practical:
Computation of marketable and marketed surplus of important
commodities; Construction of index numbers; Visit to local market to study
marketing functions performed by different agencies.
Thrust Area (Practice
sessions 3-4): Market Channel Analysis, Price Spread, and Marketing Margin
Computation


 
Module III: Market
Functionaries, Integration, and Institutional Framework


Theory:
Types and importance of agencies in agricultural marketing;
Marketing channels for different farm products — integration, efficiency, and
price spread; Meaning, definition and types of market integration; Marketing
efficiency; Ways of reducing marketing costs; Role of storage, transport, and
communication in agricultural marketing.
Practical:
Identification of marketing channels for selected commodity;
Collection of data regarding marketing costs, margins, and price spread;
Presentation of report in class.
Thrust Area (Practice
Sessions 5-6): Marketing Efficiency Measurement and Field Data Collection


 
Module IV: Government
Policy and Public Sector Institutions


Theory:
Role of Government in agricultural marketing: Public sector
institutions — CWC, SWC, FCI, CACP and DMI — their objectives and functions;
Cooperative marketing; Risk in marketing: speculation and hedging; Overview of
futures trading; Agricultural prices and policy; Administered prices; Need for
agricultural price policy; Trade: concept of international trade and its need;
Theories of absolute and comparative advantage; Present status and 
prospects of international trade in agri-commodities; GATT and
WTO; AoA and its implications on Indian agriculture; IPR; Role of government in
agricultural marketing.
Practical:
Visit to market institutions — NAFED, SWC, CWC, Cooperative
marketing society, etc. to study their organization and functioning;
Application of principles of comparative advantage of international trade.
Thrust Area (Practice Session 7-8):
Institutional Visit and Policy Analysis


 
Module V: Digital
Agricultural Marketing, Role of APMC, and Trade Policy


Theory:
Role of APMC and its relevance in the present-day context; Model
APMC Act and recent reforms; e-NAM (National Agriculture Market); Digital
marketing platforms in agriculture — Kalgudi, DeHaat, AgriMarket; Export
promotion of agricultural commodities; India's trade performance and WTO
commitments; SPS measures and their impact on Indian agri-exports; Agricultural
trade agreements and their implications.
Practical:
Case study on e-NAM and digital marketing of agri-commodities;
Analysis of agricultural export data; Study of one digital marketing platform
(Kalgudi / AgriBazaar); Preparation and presentation of commodity marketing
report.
Thrust Area (Practice
Sessions 9-10): Digital Market Platforms, Export Data Analysis, and e-NAM Case
Study
